Recorded live on the floor of Amazon Accelerate, this episode of the Serious Sellers Podcast brings together seven sellers with different backgrounds, business models, and lessons to share. Bradley Sutton starts with Sky Balukonis, who grew a disposable napkin business from roughly $40,000-$50,000 in first-year sales to a projected $1.4 million annually. Sky explains how disciplined reinvestment, careful cash flow management, and premium positioning helped an everyday product stand out. Danial Khosravi and Nick Karafilov share how they use Claude connected to Helium 10 through MCP to research keywords, improve listing copy, and prepare a data-backed presentation for a Walmart buyer. They also explain how advice from a Helium 10 Elite call with Bradley pushed them to build their Walmart presence, prepare retail-ready packaging, and generate TikTok content. Those efforts helped put them in front of a buyer, with a potential retail agreement still pending at the time of recording. items.title: #767 - Amazon Seller Secrets From China
items.excerpt: Explore the white-hat advantages and black-hat tactics used by Chinese Amazon sellers, from rapid product testing and supplier research to manufactured demand, AI imagery, and branding gaps.
items.body: Explore the white-hat advantages and black-hat tactics used by Chinese Amazon sellers, from rapid product testing and supplier research to manufactured demand, AI imagery, and branding gaps. ► Watch The Podcasts On Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/@Helium10?sub_confirmation=1 ► Instagram: instagram.com/serioussellerspodcast ► Free Amazon Seller Chrome Extension: https://h10.me/extension ► Sign Up For Helium 10: https://h10.me/signup (Use SSP10 To Save 10% For Life) ► Learn How To Sell on Amazon: https://h10.me/ft What strategies are Chinese Amazon sellers using to compete, and what can sellers elsewhere learn from them? Recorded in Shenzhen, China, Bradley Sutton sits down with experienced Amazon seller and new Helium 10 team member Shawn Su to explore the advantages, tactics, and challenges shaping one of the world’s most competitive e-commerce communities. Shawn shares his journey from two unsuccessful product launches to building two six-figure Amazon brands. He explains how he discovers overlooked opportunities using narrow price filters, minimum search-volume requirements, weak competitor images, and low title density. He also reveals why the ability to test small orders, respond to reviews, modify products, and launch improved versions quickly may be a greater advantage than lower manufacturing costs. The conversation also examines a controversial tactic involving manufactured keyword demand. Some sellers use external traffic to make previously unknown search terms appear popular before launching new FBA listings. Bradley explains why a sudden search-volume spike does not always represent organic demand—and why sellers should investigate where that traffic is coming from before entering the market.
